# mid-E co-scheduling: probe_gemm A (sequential bucket launches, shipped shape) vs B (co-resident slabs,
# one launch). Qwen3.8@2.05 layer 12, WARM_S=3, ks=2. B/A < 1 means co-scheduling wins.
# Why: live routing puts ~124 eligible experts in ONE launch at R=2048, between the measured rungs
# E=16 (B loses) and E=512 (B wins 9-16%). D17 could not decide its own operating point without this.
# generated by run_plan_close2.sh S3
== GEMM_MODE=A E=128 rows=64
gemm A (sequential bucket launches): rows 64 = NSLAB 4 x 16 rows/launch, RPAD 16, PART rows 64, threads 160 x 128 x NSLAB
case /home/treo/.cache/b70cases/midE_e128_r64: E 128 R 64 k 2560 n 640 K 2  trellis 50.00 MiB  KS 2  layout native
rev L: dpas 8 x 2 per byte-block (rows padded to 16), 1 expert/thread, 160 x 128 threads (2048 HW)
revL ks 2 rows 64 1-proj     layout native:    928.3 us    225.9 G-w/s    56.5 GB/s(trellis)   [single-launch   929.4 us]  [M 8x2, 40 tiles x 128 experts]
